explanation: Let dp[v] count ordered sequences totaling v using uint64_t cells. Sum dp[v-c] for each candidate c that fits as the final value. Unsigned additions compute residues modulo 2^64; the final guaranteed 32-bit answer is recovered exactly.
timeComplexity: O(target·c) time: target amounts each try c candidates with constant-cost uint64_t addition.
spaceComplexity: O(target) auxiliary space for target+1 fixed-width uint64_t cells.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 C++ algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Every ordered sequence has one final candidate c and a prefix totaling v-c, so summing those disjoint classes gives the exact mathematical recurrence. The uint64_t table maintains its residue modulo 2^64. Since the final true count fits a signed 32-bit integer, its residue equals that count even if unrelated intermediate totals overflow.
walkthrough: For candidates [2,3] and target 7, the only multiset is two 2s and one 3. Its orders are [2,2,3],[2,3,2],[3,2,2], so return 3. These orders count separately, unlike Combination Sum.
edgeCases: Target zero has one empty sequence.
Positive candidates make every dependency smaller.
Only the final count is guaranteed 32-bit; unsigned modular arithmetic remains valid for this addition-only recurrence.
